concepts.learning_objective: Identify a statistical question as one that is answered by collecting data that varies.
Recognise a statistical statement as a claim or summary expressed through numbers, proportions, probabilities or predictions.

topics.title: The arithmetic mean as a fair share

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate the arithmetic mean as the sum of the values divided by the number of values.
Interpret the mean as the equal share each member would get if the total were shared equally.
Distinguish a value of zero from a missing value when counting the number of values for a mean.

topics.title: Describing and comparing data with dot plots

concepts.learning_objective: Describe and compare data using its minimum, maximum, total, average and the difference between maximum and minimum.
Read and interpret a dot plot to see how data is clustered or spread out.
Find the median of sorted data with an odd or an even number of values.
Explain how an outlier affects the mean much more than the median.

topics.title: Of ends and the essence: centre and variability

concepts.learning_objective: Use the mean and median as measures of central tendency to describe the centre of data.
Describe the variability of data using its extremes and the spread between them.

topics.title: Visualising data with clustered column graphs

concepts.learning_objective: Read and explain a clustered (double) column graph that compares categories side by side.
Use the scale of a graph to convert bar lengths into values.
Make sense of a graph by first identifying what is given and then inferring from it.
Read a data table to compare values and spot trends across ages and years.
Judge whether a conclusion can be justified or generalised from the data given.
